contribution.position: My position is unchanged: the reliability evidence is incomplete. The test report (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage) and the perf report (p99 within budget at peak) are healthy, but neither exercises retry or failure-amplification conditions. The incident log shows two sev2 incidents last quarter, both traced to retry storms, so that is the failure mode that matters most for this service. Nothing provided shows this change tested under it. The ops turn calls the rollback path proven because of a restore test, 'artifact:restore-test-2026-08'. That artifact is not in the available evidence set, and the runbook (v4) says nightly backups are taken but a restore has never been tested. Until that restore result is produced and reconciled with the runbook, I treat the recovery path for a bad export run as unproven. Two small, bounded items would close the gap: (1) a retry-storm or fault-injection test result for this change, and (2) one successful restore drill from the nightly backup, or the actual restore-test artifact if it exists. Both could plausibly be done this week.
